tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms/intent (agent won't start, gateway fails, returns nothing, behaves differently in prod, which version is live) rather than internals, explicitly lists trigger contexts including ones where the user doesn't name the underlying concepts ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name'), and is concise (a few sentences).
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (what AWS, Bedrock, or runtimes are) and jumps directly to domain-specific procedures, check-ids, API calls, and edge cases specific to AgentCore/Bedrock Agents. It is dense but all content is domain-specific and actionable.
tests.evidence: Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under `references/`: `checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001..014...) and `checks-agents.md` (LLM-AGT-001..011...)

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (full API quirks, metric thresholds, check catalogs) live in references/ files and are only summarized or pointed to in the body via router table rows; no large reference tables are embedded in the body itself.
tests.evidence: How to read each API and metric is in `references/collection-reference.md`. Load it with any row.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All 8 files in references/ are linked with markdown link syntax in the body (router table, appendix, error handling sections).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The router table ties each reference file link to a specific operator symptom/condition, clearly indicating when to load each file, and other links (router-details, runtime-sessions, api-quirks) are tied to specific triggering scenarios.
tests.evidence: | AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | `ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` for status, version, role ARN | `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference file links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (IAM simulation order, alias resolution before concluding production, read-only guardrails) are given exact prescriptive steps, while broader judgment calls (hypothesis framing, migration advisory wording) allow for agent reasoning with explained rationale.
tests.evidence: Do not conclude what production runs until the alias is resolved (Step 2) — a prepared DRAFT is not what the alias serves.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple options exist (e.g., migration paths), a clear default/primary is designated (AgentCore harness) with the alternative noted as secondary, and procedures generally specify the first/primary API read.
tests.evidence: recommend migrating via the **AgentCore harness** (config-based, closest analog) or **code-defined agents on AgentCore**

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach a generalizable approach for reviewing any AgentCore runtime or Bedrock Agent (reading role, simulating actions, checking VPC, gateway, etc.) rather than being tied to one specific instance/task.
tests.evidence: Step 2: Simulate the runtime role with `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` for every action it exercises...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' section plus 'Error Handling' documenting non-obvious API quirks (alias vs DRAFT, no-datapoints vs zero, denied permission vs absent resource) that function as gotchas.
tests.evidence: "GetAgent shows PREPARED, so that config is what production runs." An agent's live behaviour is its alias → version resolution...

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured review reports and explicitly provides/links a template for this purpose.
tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the template is stored in assets/ and referenced.
tests.evidence: `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md` — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced multiple times in the body.
tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load

tests.evidence: When a full report is requested, the output follows `assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md`.

tests.name: Asset path format

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: Both procedures (AgentCore review and Bedrock Agents Classic review) are presented as checkbox checklists with '- [ ] Step N:' format, consistent with the ordered, dependent nature of the tasks.
tests.evidence: - [ ] Step 1: Read the runtime with `bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes` / `GetAgentRuntime` — status, version, endpoint...

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation checklist ('Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output') instructing the agent to check findings, evidence, and masking before presenting.
tests.evidence: Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
